% 736-readline-specials: verifies \readline keeps backslashes, braces and comment chars verbatim from a generated file while \read tokenizes them: box0 typesets the verbatim meaning, box1 the tokenized control meaning.
\input prelude
\font\myrm=cmr10
\catcode`\%=12
\immediate\openout1=ls736data.txt
\immediate\write1{a\string\foo{b} %x tail}
\immediate\write1{a\string\foo{b} %x tail}
\catcode`\%=14
\immediate\closeout1
\openin0=ls736data.txt
\endlinechar=-1 \readline0 to\lnV \endlinechar=13
\message{736 verbatim=\meaning\lnV}
\read0 to\lnT
\message{736 tokenized=\meaning\lnT}
\closein0
\setbox0=\hbox{\myrm\meaning\lnV}
\setbox1=\hbox{\myrm\meaning\lnT}
\lsshipbox0
\lsshipbox1
\end
